claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about hair cell development.

claims.claim: Sustained contact with sensory axons influences the maintenance and stability of presynaptic ribbons in hair cells.
claims.source: However, sustained contact with the sensory axon influences the maintenance and stability of ribbons (Suli et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The average number of CTBP punctae is reduced in sema7a-/- mutants compared to controls.
claims.source: This result implies that the formation of new presynaptic ribbons is not perturbed in the mutants, even though there are on average fewer CTBP punctae (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The average area of presynaptic densities is reduced in sema7a-/- mutants compared to controls.
claims.source: Measurement of the areas of CTBP punctae also showed similar distributions in both genotypes (Figure 6E and F) but the average area of presynaptic densities was reduced in the mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Postsynaptic densities occur more extensively on loops than on bare terminals of the sensory arbor network.
claims.source: Comparison of the topological features of the network with the spatial locations of the MAGUK punctae revealed that the postsynaptic densities occur more extensively on the loops than on the bare terminals (Figure 6G, Video 20). We measured 567 MAGUK punctae from 16 sensory arbor networks, where 531 punctae were located on the loops and only 36 punctae on the bare terminals (Figure 6H).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6H.

claims.claim: MAGUK punctae predominantly aggregate near nodes and their density diminishes moving farther from nodes.
claims.source: Furthermore, the MAGUK punctae predominantly aggregate near the node and their density sharply diminishes moving farther from the node (Figure 6I, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through spatial analysis shown in Figure 6I.

claims.claim: At 4 dpf, 68.3% of hair cells in control neuromasts are associated with at least one MAGUK punctum, compared to 37.5% in sema7a-/- mutants.
claims.source: At 4 dpf, 68.3% of the hair cells in the control neuromasts were associated with at least one MAGUK punctum. In the sema7a-/- mutant this value fell to 37.5% (Figure 6L and M).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6L and M.

claims.claim: The average number of MAGUK punctae is reduced in sema7a-/- mutants compared to controls.
claims.source: The average number of MAGUK punctae also declined in the mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G–I).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: As control neuromasts mature from 2 dpf to 4 dpf, MAGUK punctae shift toward smaller sizes.
claims.source: As control neuromasts matured from 2 dpf to 4 dpf, the MAGUK punctae showed a shift toward smaller sizes, suggesting that the postsynaptic structure fragmented into smaller entities as observed in other excitatory synapses (Taschenberger et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of MAGUK punctae areas and comparison to other synapses.

claims.claim: At 4 dpf, 77.5% of hair cells in control neuromasts have postsynaptic densities with areas between 0.10 µm2 and 0.40 µm2, compared to 42.5% in sema7a-/- mutants.
claims.source: At 4 dpf, 77.5% of the hair cells in the control neuromasts had postsynaptic densities with areas between 0.10 µm2 and 0.40 µm2. In the sema7a-/- mutant the corresponding value was only 42.5% (Figure 6N and O).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6N and O.

claims.claim: The average area of MAGUK punctae is reduced in sema7a-/- mutants compared to controls.
claims.source: The average area of MAGUK punctae was also reduced in the mutants compared to the controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 1J–L, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Sema7A acts as an important mediator of sensory arbor reorganization and microcircuit assembly in the zebrafish lateral line.
claims.source: Here, we report that Semaphorin7A (Sema7A) acts as an important mediator of these processes.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claims.claim: Sensory axons in Sema7A mutants display aberrant arborizations with disorganized network topology and diminished contacts to hair cells.
claims.source: In contrast to those of wild-type animals, the sensory axons in Sema7A mutants display aberrant arborizations with disorganized network topology and diminished contacts to hair cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of findings.

claims.claim: Sema7A likely functions both as a juxtracrine and as a secreted cue to pattern neural circuitry during sensory organ development.
claims.source: Our findings propose that Sema7A likely functions both as a juxtracrine and as a secreted cue to pattern neural circuitry during sensory organ development.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claims.claim: Semaphorins are important regulators of axonal growth and target finding during the patterning of diverse neural circuits.
claims.source: Semaphorins are important regulators of axonal growth and target finding during the patterning of diverse neural circuits (Carulli et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claims.claim: Sema7A is the only semaphorin molecule anchored to the cell membrane by a GPI linker.
claims.source: Among these, Semaphorin7A (Sema7A) is the only molecule that is anchored to the outer leaflet of the lipid bilayer of the cell membrane by a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) linker (Yazdani and Terman, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claims.claim: Unlike many other semaphorins which act as repulsive cues, Sema7A is involved in promoting axon growth.
claims.source: Unlike many other semaphorins, which act as repulsive cues (de Winter et al., 2016; Coate et al., 2015), Sema7A is involved in promoting axon growth (Jeroen Pasterkamp et al., 2003)
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Sema7A imparts directional signals by interacting with integrin and plexin families of receptors on pathfinding axons.
claims.source: and imparting directional signals by interacting with the integrin and plexin families of receptors residing on the pathfinding axons (Carcea et al., 2014; Inoue et al., 2018; Inoue et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Sema7A likely occurs in vivo in both GPI-anchored and soluble forms.
claims.source: Sema7A likely occurs in vivo in both GPI-anchored and soluble forms (Morote-Garcia et al., 2012; Nishide and Kumanogoh, 2018; Köhler et al., 2020)
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Both GPI-anchored and soluble forms of Sema7A can induce directed axonal outgrowth in neuronal explants.
claims.source: and studies of neuronal explants confirm that both forms can induce directed axonal outgrowth (Jeroen Pasterkamp et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The GPI anchor of Sema7A is proposed to be cleaved by GPI-specific phospholipases or matrix metalloproteases to release Sema7A into the extracellular environment.
claims.source: Furthermore, it has been proposed that the GPI anchor is cleaved by membrane-resident GPI-specific phospholipases (GPI-PLs) or matrix metalloproteases to release the Sema7A into the extracellular environment and thus regulate dynamic cellular processes (Pham et al., 2017; Xie and Wang, 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data identified the sema7a gene to be highly expressed in hair cells of the zebrafish lateral line.
claims.source: Analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data identified the semaphorin7a (sema7a) gene to be highly expressed in hair cells of that organ (Lush et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to the single-cell RNA sequencing study.

claims.claim: In the mouse olfactory system, GPI-anchored Sema7A is enriched in olfactory sensory axons and mediates sustained interaction with dendrites to establish synapses.
claims.source: In the mouse olfactory system, GPI-anchored Sema7A is enriched in olfactory sensory axons and mediates sustained interaction with the dendrites of mitral and tufted cells in the olfactory bulb to establish synapses (Inoue et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claims.claim: In developing mouse Purkinje cells, GPI-anchored Sema7A regulates the elimination of synapses onto climbing fibers.
claims.source: In the developing mouse brain–particularly in Purkinje cells–GPI-anchored Sema7A instead regulates the elimination of synapses onto climbing fibers (Uesaka et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The role of anchored Sema7A in regulating synaptic architecture varies according to cell type and developmental stage.
claims.source: The role of anchored Sema7A in regulating synaptic architecture can thus vary according to the cell type and developmental stage.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the different roles observed in different systems.

claims.claim: Lateral-line sensory axons likely utilize integrinβ1 and plexinC1 signaling pathways to sense and respond to Sema7A.
claims.source: Recent studies have begun to dissect the molecular mechanisms of semaphorin signaling in axonal navigation. In explants derived from the murine olfactory bulb, Sema7A interacts directly with integrinβ1 to trigger downstream signaling effectors involving focal adhesion kinase and mitogen-activated protein kinases, which are critical regulators of the cytoskeletal network during axonal pathfinding (Jeroen Pasterkamp et al., 2003; Myers and Gomez, 2011). Moreover, the interaction between Sema7A and its receptor plexinC1 activates the rac1-cdc42-PAK pathway, which alters the actin network to promote axonal guidance and synapse formation (Inoue et al., 2018; O'Donnell et al., 2009). We speculate that lateral-line sensory axons utilize similar mechanisms to sense and respond to Sema7A in the establishment of microcircuits with hair cells.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on mechanisms observed in other systems.

claims.claim: The decrease in average number and area of CTBP punctae in sema7a mutants likely reflects decreased stability of presynaptic ribbons due to lack of contact between sensory axons and hair cells.
claims.source: We propose that the decrease in average number and area of CTBP punctae likely reflects decreased stability of the presynaptic ribbons owing to lack of contact between the sensory axons and the hair cells.
claims.evidence: This is proposed as an interpretation of the observed data.

claims.claim: It is unlikely that Sema7A signaling directly induces the formation of presynaptic ribbons because GPI-anchored Sema7A lacks a cytosolic domain.
claims.source: Because GPI-anchored Sema7A lacks a cytosolic domain, it is unlikely that Sema7A signaling directly induces the formation of presynaptic ribbons.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural properties of GPI-anchored proteins.

claims.claim: Abnormalities in postsynaptic structure of sema7a-/- mutants arise from reduced contact between hair cells and sensory axons, perturbed topological attributes of the sensory circuit, or lack of Sema7A-GPI-mediated juxtracrine signaling.
claims.source: We speculate that the abnormalities in the postsynaptic structure of the sema7a-/- mutants arose from reduced contact between the hair cells and the sensory axons and perturbed topological attributes of the sensory circuit or from the lack of Sema7A-GPI-mediated juxtracrine signaling onto the apposed neurite terminals (Inoue et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is speculated as an explanation for the observed phenotype.

claims.claim: A local Sema7Asec diffusive cue likely consolidates sensory arbors at the hair cell cluster.
claims.source: Our results suggest a potential mechanism for hair cell innervation in which a local Sema7Asec diffusive cue likely consolidates the sensory arbors at the hair cell cluster
claims.evidence: This is proposed as a mechanism based on the experimental results.

claims.claim: Membrane-anchored Sema7A-GPI guides microcircuit topology and synapse assembly.
claims.source: and the membrane-anchored Sema7A-GPI molecule guides microcircuit topology and synapse assembly.
claims.evidence: This is proposed as a mechanism based on the experimental results.

claims.claim: The precise patterning of the sensory arbor network with characteristic looping behaviors may contribute to the network's ability to gather sensory inputs and transmit information.
claims.source: The preferential localization of the postsynaptic aggregates in the loops and an enrichment near the nodes of the arbor network suggest that the precise patterning of the network—with characteristic looping behaviors—is not merely a byproduct of neuromast architecture, but may contribute to the network's ability to gather sensory inputs through properly placed postsynaptic aggregates and to faithfully transmit sensory information to higher processing centers in the hindbrain (Valera et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is proposed based on the observed correlation between topology and synapse distribution.

claims.claim: Diverse chemoattractive factors including Sema7A occur uniformly between hair cell polarities.
claims.source: Although sensory axons are strict selectors of hair cell polarity and form synapses accordingly (Nagiel et al., 2008), diverse chemoattractant cues including Sema7A occur uniformly between hair cell polarities (Germanà et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Unbiased attractive signals bring sensory arbors toward hair cells, after which polarity-specific molecules dictate final association between axonal terminals and hair cells.
claims.source: It seems likely that unbiased attractive signals bring sensory arbors toward hair cells, after which polarity-specific molecules on hair cell surfaces dictate the final association between axonal terminal and hair cells.
claims.evidence: This is proposed as a model based on the observed expression patterns.

claims.claim: Notch-delta signaling and its downstream effectors regulate hair cell polarity and innervation pattern.
claims.source: Notch-delta signaling and its downstream effectors regulate hair cell polarity and the innervation pattern (Jacobo et al., 2019; Dow et al., 2018; Ji et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: During early development of the posterior lateral line, growth cones of sensory axons intimately associate with the prosensory primordium.
claims.source: During early development of the posterior lateral line, the growth cones of sensory axons intimately associate with the prosensory primordium that deposits neuromasts along the lateral surface of the larva (Gilmour et al., 2004; Metcalfe, 1985).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Growth of sensory fibers with the primordium is regulated by diverse neurotrophic factors expressed in the primordium.
claims.source: The growth of the sensory fibers with the primordium is regulated by diverse neurotrophic factors expressed in the primordium (Gasanov et al., 2015; Schuster et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Impairing brain-derived or glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factors and their receptors perturbs directed axonal motility and innervation of hair cells.
claims.source: Impairing brain-derived or glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factors and their receptors perturbs directed axonal motility and innervation of hair cells (Gasanov et al., 2015; Schuster et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Lateral-line hair cells are particularly enriched in brain-derived neurotrophic factor.
claims.source: Lateral-line hair cells are particularly enriched in brain-derived neurotrophic factor (Germanà et al., 2010) and other chemotropic cues (Figure 7).
claims.evidence: This is stated with citation and shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Sensory axons of sema7a-/- mutants reliably branch from the lateral-line nerve to reach hair cell clusters.
claims.source: Because the sensory axons of sema7a-/- mutants reliably branch from the lateral-line nerve to reach hair cell clusters, these chemoattractive factors might compensate in part for the absence of Sema7A function.
claims.evidence: This is observed in the mutant phenotype analysis.

results.result: The zebrafish sema7a gene produces two transcript variants: Sema7A-GPI (full-length, GPI-anchored) and Sema7Asec (truncated, potentially secreted). Both transcripts encode an N-terminal signal sequence and conserved Sema domain, and both are present in hair cells of lateral-line neuromasts.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 are well-supported by RT-PCR data (Figure 1B-D) demonstrating the presence of both transcripts in FACS-sorted hair cells. The structural characterization is consistent with known semaphorin biology, though the secretion of Sema7Asec remains conjectural (C3).

results.result: Sema7A protein is specifically localized in hair cells with enrichment in the subapical (Golgi) region and progressive accumulation at the basal surface during development (2-4 dpf). Basal Sema7A accumulation positively correlates with sensory arbor association.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C14 are supported by immunolabeling data (Figure 1E-I) showing Sema7A localization and quantitative analysis demonstrating developmental changes and correlation with sensory arbor contact. The Golgi localization (C10) is confirmed by GM130 colocalization. Statistical significance is demonstrated for developmental changes (C8) and correlation with arbor association (C14).

results.result: The sema7asa24691 mutant contains a premature stop codon in the conserved sema domain, resulting in 61% reduction in Sema7A protein levels without affecting hair cell number or mechanotransduction function.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C20 are supported by molecular characterization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), immunolabeling quantification showing 61% reduction (C17), and FM 4-64 uptake assays demonstrating normal mechanotransduction (C19-C20). The lack of effect on hair cell number (C18) is appropriately documented as a control.

results.result: Loss of Sema7A causes aberrant sensory arbor arborization with projections extending away from hair cell clusters. In sema7a-/- mutants, only 67±2% of arbors contact hair cells at 4 dpf compared to 90±1% in controls.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C27 are strongly supported by 3D imaging and skeletonized network analysis (Figure 2F-M). Quantitative measurements show significant reduction in arbor-hair cell contact (C26-C27) and increased arbor extension beyond cluster boundaries (C25). The combined analysis of 27 control and 27 mutant neuromasts provides robust statistical support.

results.result: Sema7A regulates multiple topological features of the sensory arbor network including node-degree distribution, loop formation preference, and arbor curvature. In controls, arbors >30 µm form loops with 4 nodes and 30-40 µm length, while mutants show disrupted topology with more bare terminals and reduced curvature.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C38 are supported by comprehensive topological analysis (Figure 3, Table 1) with statistical validation. The length-dependent loop formation rules (C31-C34) and loop characteristics (C35-C36) show significant differences between genotypes at 4 dpf. Chi-square and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests confirm statistical significance (Table 1). The analysis represents a novel quantitative approach to characterizing neural circuit topology.

results.result: Ectopic expression of Sema7Asec induces robust axonal projections from sensory arbor networks toward the ectopic source. In all 22 cases examined, projections extended 27-143 µm with near-perfect correlation between projection and source-path length, remaining within 3.5±0.7 µm of the source.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C44 are strongly supported by ectopic expression experiments (Figure 4A-G) with quantitative measurements from 18 integration events. The nearly perfect correlation (C43) and low projection-proximity distance (C44) demonstrate that Sema7Asec is sufficient for long-range axon guidance. The distinction between accessible (muscle progenitors) and inaccessible (deep myofibers) targets (C40-C41) provides important mechanistic insight.

results.result: Axonal projections from the posterior lateral-line nerve respond to ectopic Sema7Asec sources between neuromasts, with neurites showing high motility and maintaining contact for 1-8 hours.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C47 are supported by imaging of 7 integration events between neuromasts (Figure 4H-J) and time-lapse microscopy (Videos 13-16). The dynamic behavior of neurites (C46) and sustained contact (C47) demonstrate that Sema7Asec responsiveness is intrinsic to sensory axons and does not require the neuromast microenvironment.

results.result: Ectopic expression of Sema7A-GPI does not induce sensory axons to leave the arbor network and approach ectopic sources, suggesting that Sema7A-GPI functions at the surfaces of expressing cells unlike its secreted counterpart.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C49 are supported by negative results from 15 ectopic Sema7A-GPI integration events (Figure 5). The lack of long-range attraction contrasts with Sema7Asec results and supports the interpretation that GPI-anchored Sema7A functions through contact-dependent mechanisms. However, the study does not directly test contact-dependent function of Sema7A-GPI.

results.result: Presynaptic ribbon formation is intrinsic to hair cells but their maintenance requires sensory axon contact. In sema7a-/- mutants, the average number and area of CTBP punctae (presynaptic markers) are reduced compared to controls, though the distribution pattern is similar.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C53 are supported by CTBP immunolabeling and quantification (Figure 6A-F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-F). The similar distribution patterns (Figure 6C-F) but reduced average number and area (C52-C53) support the interpretation that ribbon formation is not disrupted but stability is reduced. C50-C51 are appropriately cited to prior work.

results.result: Postsynaptic densities (MAGUK punctae) occur preferentially on loops rather than bare terminals and aggregate near nodes. In sema7a-/- mutants at 4 dpf, only 37.5% of hair cells have MAGUK punctae compared to 68.3% in controls, with reduced average number and area.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C60 are supported by MAGUK immunolabeling and spatial analysis (Figure 6G-O, Figure 6—figure supplement 1G-L). The preferential localization on loops (531/567 punctae, C54) and near nodes (C55) links network topology to synapse distribution. The significant reductions in mutants (C56-C60) are well-documented with appropriate statistical analysis. The developmental shift toward smaller punctae (C58) is appropriately cited to prior work on excitatory synapses.

results.result: Sema7A acts as an important mediator of sensory arbor reorganization and microcircuit assembly in the zebrafish lateral line, likely functioning both as a juxtracrine (GPI-anchored) and secreted cue to pattern neural circuitry during sensory organ development.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C63 represent the main conclusions of the study and are well-supported by the collective evidence from mutant phenotype analysis (aberrant arborization, C62), ectopic expression experiments (differential effects of Sema7Asec vs. Sema7A-GPI), and synaptic defects. The dual-function model (C63) is a reasonable synthesis of the data, though direct demonstration of GPI-anchored function would strengthen the conclusion.

results.result: The authors propose that lateral-line sensory axons utilize integrinβ1 and plexinC1 signaling pathways to respond to Sema7A, and that synaptic defects in mutants arise from reduced contact, perturbed topology, or lack of juxtracrine signaling. GPI-anchored Sema7A is unlikely to directly induce presynaptic ribbon formation due to lack of a cytosolic domain.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C78 are speculative interpretations based on mechanisms observed in other systems (cited appropriately). While the reasoning is sound (C77 regarding GPI-anchored proteins), these mechanisms are not directly tested in this study. The proposals are plausible but require experimental validation through receptor manipulation or rescue experiments.

results.result: The authors propose a mechanism where secreted Sema7Asec consolidates sensory arbors at hair cell clusters while membrane-anchored Sema7A-GPI guides microcircuit topology and synapse assembly. The precise network patterning may contribute to sensory input gathering and information transmission.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 represent a synthesis of the experimental findings into a coherent model. The model is well-supported by the differential effects of ectopic Sema7Asec (long-range attraction) vs. Sema7A-GPI (no long-range effect), combined with the correlation between topology and synapse distribution. However, the functional significance (C81) remains speculative and would benefit from physiological studies.

results.result: Multiple chemoattractive factors including Sema7A, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, and others are expressed in hair cells and may provide unbiased attractive signals, with polarity-specific molecules dictating final axon-hair cell association. These factors may partially compensate for Sema7A loss in mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C89 appropriately contextualize the findings within the broader literature on lateral-line development. The expression of multiple guidance factors (C82, C88, Figure 7) and the observation that mutant axons still reach hair cell clusters (C89) support the compensation hypothesis. The model of unbiased attraction followed by polarity-specific refinement (C83) is reasonable but speculative. Citations to prior work (C84-C87) are appropriate.

results.result: Background claims establishing that semaphorins regulate axon guidance, Sema7A is uniquely GPI-anchored among semaphorins, can exist in both anchored and soluble forms, and has diverse roles in different neural systems including the mouse olfactory system and cerebellum.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C74 provide appropriate background context and are properly cited to prior literature. These establish the rationale for investigating Sema7A in the lateral line system and provide comparative context for interpreting the results. The citations appear accurate and relevant.

results.result: The zebrafish sema7a gene produces two transcript variants: Sema7A-GPI (membrane-anchored) and Sema7Asec (secreted), both containing the conserved Sema domain and expressed in hair cells of lateral-line neuromasts.
results.evaluation: Multiple reviewers acknowledge the identification of two Sema7A isoforms without questioning this finding. One reviewer notes 'they added evidence that hair cells express both Sema7A isoforms,' confirming acceptance of this result. The RT-PCR and single-cell RNA sequencing data supporting transcript identification are not challenged.

results.result: Sema7A protein is specifically localized in hair cells, enriched in the subapical Golgi region and increasingly accumulating at the basal region during development (2-4 dpf), with basal accumulation correlating positively with sensory arbor association.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praise the localization data. One states 'The availability of Sema7a antibody is a big plus, as it allows to address the endogenous protein localization.' Another notes the study 'show[s] that Sema7a protein is present during neuromast maturation and localized, in part, to the base of hair cells.' No concerns are raised about the immunolabeling or localization findings.

results.result: The sema7a mutant allele contains a premature stop codon that reduces Sema7A protein by 61% but does not affect hair cell number or mechanotransduction function (FM 4-64 uptake).
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the mutant characterization without objection. One reviewer notes 'they...showed that membrane bound Sema7A does not have long range effects on guidance...and analyzed other features of the hair cells that revealed no strong phenotypes,' indicating acceptance of the control experiments showing normal hair cell function. The mutant validation is treated as solid.

results.result: In sema7a mutants, sensory axons display aberrant arborization patterns with wayward projections extending far beyond hair cell clusters, resulting in significantly reduced contact (67% vs 90% at 4 dpf) compared to controls where arbors consolidate within hair cell boundaries.
results.evaluation: All reviewers affirm this core finding. One states 'the sensory axons in Sema7A mutants display aberrant arborizations with disorganized network topology and diminished contacts to hair cells.' Another notes 'loss of both Sema7a isoforms causes abnormal axon terminal structure.' The quantitative analysis of arbor-hair cell contact is accepted without challenge.

results.result: Loss of Sema7A disrupts multiple topological features of sensory arbor networks including node-degree distribution, the transition from bare terminals to loops, arbor length-dependent topological choices, loop structure (nodes per loop and contour length), and arbor curvature.
results.evaluation: Reviewers consistently praise the topological analysis. One states 'They provide highly quantitative analysis of the lateral line terminal arborization to show that a number of specific topological parameters are affected in mutants.' Another notes 'The quantification of the arbor topology should be useful to people in the field.' The sophisticated network analysis is explicitly commended without methodological concerns.

results.result: Ectopic expression of secreted Sema7Asec induces robust, long-range axonal projections (27-142 μm) from sensory arbors toward the ectopic source, with projections showing dynamic motility and sustained contact lasting 1-8 hours.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the ectopic Sema7Asec attraction data. One notes 'overexpression of the secreted form of Sema7a specifically can elicit axon terminal outgrowth to an ectopic Sema7a expressing cell.' Another states the authors 'demonstrated how axons behave close to ectopic Sema7A,' indicating acceptance of the time-lapse and quantitative measurements of projection behavior.

results.result: Ectopic expression of membrane-anchored Sema7A-GPI does not induce long-range axonal projections, suggesting it functions locally at cell surfaces unlike the secreted form.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this control experiment. One states the authors 'showed that membrane bound Sema7A does not have long range effects on guidance,' confirming acceptance of the differential behavior between the two isoforms. This finding is treated as important evidence for distinct functional roles.

results.result: The average number and area of presynaptic ribbons (CTBP punctae) are reduced in sema7a mutants compared to controls, though the distribution of ribbon sizes remains similar.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the presynaptic phenotype. One states 'they show that loss of Sema7a causes decreased number and size of both the pre- and post-synapse.' The presynaptic analysis is not questioned, though reviewers note the evidence for direct Sema7A involvement in synapse formation is less conclusive (addressed in mechanistic claims).

results.result: Postsynaptic densities (MAGUK punctae) preferentially localize to loops rather than bare terminals and aggregate near nodes; in sema7a mutants, fewer hair cells have postsynaptic densities (37.5% vs 68.3% at 4 dpf), and the average number and area of MAGUK punctae are reduced.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the postsynaptic findings. One notes 'loss of Sema7a causes decreased number and size of both the pre- and post-synapse.' The correlation between network topology and synapse distribution is accepted. The quantitative analysis of MAGUK punctae distribution and the mutant phenotype are not challenged.

results.result: Sema7A acts as a mediator of sensory arbor reorganization and microcircuit assembly, with the secreted form (Sema7Asec) consolidating arbors at hair cell clusters and the membrane-anchored form (Sema7A-GPI) guiding microcircuit topology and synapse assembly.
results.evaluation: Reviewers express mixed views on the mechanistic conclusions. One states 'the findings point to the idea that the diffusible form of sema7a may influence how axons grow within the neuromast and that the GPI-linked form of sema7a may subsequently impact how synapses form, though additional work is needed to strongly link each form to its proposed effect.' Another notes 'The evidence supporting Sema7a's juxtracrine vs. secreted role and involvement in synapse formation in hair cells is less conclusive.' The overall role is accepted but specific isoform functions require further validation.

results.result: The decrease in presynaptic ribbons in sema7a mutants likely reflects decreased stability due to lack of axon-hair cell contact rather than direct Sema7A signaling, and postsynaptic abnormalities may arise from reduced contact, perturbed topology, or lack of juxtracrine signaling.
results.evaluation: These mechanistic interpretations are speculative and reviewers note the evidence is incomplete. One reviewer states 'The evidence supporting Sema7a's...involvement in synapse formation in hair cells is less conclusive.' The authors themselves present these as speculations, and reviewers implicitly accept them as reasonable hypotheses requiring further testing rather than established conclusions.

results.result: The precise patterning of sensory arbor networks with characteristic looping may contribute to sensory information processing, and unbiased attractive signals like Sema7A may bring arbors to hair cells before polarity-specific molecules dictate final associations.
results.evaluation: These are interpretive claims about functional significance that reviewers do not explicitly evaluate. The authors present them as speculative models based on observed correlations. While the underlying data (topology-synapse correlation) are accepted, the functional implications and hierarchical model of guidance cues remain hypothetical.

results.result: Background claims about Sema7A biology, semaphorin function, hair cell development, and lateral line neurotrophic factors based on published literature and established knowledge.
results.evaluation: These are literature-based contextual claims that reviewers do not question. They serve as background for the study and are supported by appropriate citations. Reviewers accept the framing of Sema7A as a unique GPI-anchored semaphorin and the developmental context of the lateral line system.

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluate the identification of Sema7A isoforms (C1-C5) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes RT-PCR data from Figure 1B-D and notes C3 (secretion) remains conjectural. Peer review confirms acceptance without challenge, noting added evidence for hair cell expression of both isoforms. Strong agreement on transcript identification, though peer review also includes C6 (protein localization) which OpenEval addresses separately.

Both evaluate Sema7A localization data (C7-C14) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details immunolabeling, Golgi colocalization (C10), developmental changes (C8), and correlation with arbor contact (C14). Peer review praises antibody availability and endogenous protein localization during neuromast maturation. Complete agreement on the quality and validity of localization findings.

Perfect alignment on mutant characterization (C15-C20) as SUPPORTED. Both accept the 61% reduction in Sema7A (C17), normal mechanotransduction (C19-C20), and lack of effect on hair cell number (C18). Peer review notes these control experiments revealed 'no strong phenotypes,' confirming the mutant validation is solid.

Complete agreement on aberrant arborization phenotype (C21-C27) as SUPPORTED. Both emphasize quantitative 3D imaging showing reduced arbor-hair cell contact (C26-C27) and increased extension beyond boundaries (C25). Peer review affirms 'disorganized network topology and diminished contacts to hair cells' as a core finding accepted without challenge.

Strong consensus on topological analysis (C28-C38) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the novel quantitative approach with statistical validation (Chi-square, K-S tests). Peer review explicitly praises the 'highly quantitative analysis' and notes the methodology 'should be useful to people in the field.' No methodological concerns from either evaluation.

Both evaluate ectopic Sema7Asec experiments (C39-C44) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the nearly perfect correlation (C43) and quantitative measurements from 18 integration events. Peer review confirms acceptance of long-range attraction by secreted form and time-lapse documentation. OpenEval also includes C45-C47 (inter-neuromast experiments) which peer review addresses in the same result.

OpenEval evaluates inter-neuromast ectopic expression (C45-C47) as SUPPORTED, emphasizing dynamic neurite behavior and sustained contact from time-lapse microscopy. Peer review groups these claims with C39-C44, noting authors 'demonstrated how axons behave close to ectopic Sema7A.' Both accept the evidence but organize it differently.

Perfect agreement on Sema7A-GPI negative results (C48-C49) as SUPPORTED. Both note the lack of long-range attraction from 15 integration events contrasts with Sema7Asec, supporting distinct functional roles. OpenEval notes the study doesn't directly test contact-dependent function; peer review treats this as important evidence for differential isoform behavior.

Both evaluate presynaptic phenotype (C52-C53) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details reduced ribbon number and area with CTBP immunolabeling, noting formation is not disrupted but stability is reduced. Peer review accepts 'decreased number and size' of presynapse, though notes evidence for direct Sema7A involvement in synapse formation is less conclusive.

Complete alignment on postsynaptic analysis (C54-C60) as SUPPORTED. Both accept MAGUK punctae preferential localization on loops (531/567), correlation with topology, and significant reductions in mutants. Peer review confirms the topology-synapse correlation without challenge. Quantitative spatial analysis is accepted by both.

Divergent evaluations of main conclusions (C61-C63). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the dual-function model is reasonable synthesis though direct demonstration of GPI function would strengthen it. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, stating 'additional work is needed to strongly link each form to its proposed effect' and evidence for specific isoform functions is 'less conclusive.'

Agreement on mechanistic speculation (C75-C78) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are speculative interpretations from other systems, not directly tested here, requiring experimental validation. Peer review similarly notes evidence is incomplete and these are reasonable hypotheses requiring further testing rather than established conclusions.

Divergent evaluations of synthesis model (C79-C81). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the model is well-supported by differential ectopic expression effects, though functional significance (C81) is speculative. Peer review groups these with C61-C63 and rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the need for additional validation of isoform-specific functions.

Partial overlap on interpretive claims. OpenEval evaluates C79-C81 (synthesis model) as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses C81-C84 (functional significance and guidance hierarchy) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative models based on correlations. Both recognize the underlying data are solid but functional implications remain hypothetical.

Both evaluate contextual/literature claims (C82-C89 in OpenEval, broader set in peer review) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate contextualization within lateral-line literature and reasonable compensation hypothesis. Peer review accepts these as background framing without question. Both treat citations as appropriate and relevant.

Strong overlap on background claims (C64-C74). OpenEval evaluates these as SUPPORTED, noting they provide appropriate context and rationale with accurate citations. Peer review groups these with other literature-based claims (C50-C51, C75, C85-C89) and accepts them as unquestioned background. Both affirm the contextual framing is solid.

Minor overlap on C50-C51 (ribbon synapse background). OpenEval includes these with presynaptic data (C52-C53) and rates SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citation to prior work. Peer review groups C50-C51 with other literature-based contextual claims and accepts them without question as background information.

Minimal overlap on C75 (mechanistic speculation about receptors). OpenEval includes this with C76-C78 and rates UNCERTAIN as speculative interpretation from other systems. Peer review groups C75 with extensive background claims and rates the entire set SUPPORTED as literature context. Different scopes of evaluation.
